intervals.label: under construction
intervals.quote: NUCLEUS is an experiment under construction based on ultra-low threshold (20 eVnr) cryogenic calorimeters, operated at tens-of-mK temperatures.

intervals.label: commissioning (technical run)
intervals.quote: incorporating a data-driven treatment of the low-energy excess (LEE) observed during commissioning

name: NUCLEUS cryogenic calorimeter array
notes: Mass figures differ by publication phase: the 2017 founding concept paper describes a combined CaWO4 + Al2O3 array of about 10 g total; the 2026 sensitivity-projection paper describes the current 'Technical Run' target as 7 g of CaWO4 specifically. Both are recorded; neither supersedes the other in the sources fetched.

placements.quote: operated at the Chooz nuclear power plant in France

target_mass.note: This is the Technical Run target mass from the most recent (2026) sourced paper. The original 2017 concept paper described a combined CaWO4 + Al2O3 array of about 10 g total (src:cevns-nucleus-founding-2017); recorded here in `note` rather than as a second value.
target_mass.quote: For the Technical Run with a 7 g CaWO4 target, we find competitive sensitivity to several scenarios beyond the Standard Model

threshold.note: eV(nr) = nuclear-recoil-equivalent electron-volts; not a standard energy unit distinct from eV, recorded here as eV.

summary.plain: A tiny, extraordinarily sensitive detector made of a few grams of crystal, cooled almost to absolute zero, designed to feel the faint nudge of a reactor antineutrino bouncing off a whole atomic nucleus at the lowest energies yet attempted.
summary.technical: NUCLEUS cryogenic calorimeter array: gram-scale CaWO4 (and, in the original concept, Al2O3) target crystals operated at millikelvin temperatures with a ~20 eV(nr) nuclear-recoil threshold; Technical Run target mass 7 g CaWO4; under construction by 2022, in commissioning (with an observed low-energy excess under study) by 2026.

technology.value: gram-scale CaWO4/Al2O3 cryogenic calorimeters with active background discrimination, operated at millikelvin temperatures
